preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 100000 for line in stdin.splitlines() for x in line.split() if x.isdigit())
preconditions.description: All integers in input are within bounds 1 ≤ n, m, d ≤ 100000 and 1 ≤ pi ≤ n for affected settlements.

preconditions.expression: len(stdin.splitlines()) == n + 1 and 1 <= m <= n and 0 <= d <= n - 1
preconditions.description: Input has exactly n+1 lines: first line with n, m, d; second line with m affected settlements; and n-1 lines with path pairs.

preconditions.expression: len(set(p for p in stdin.splitlines()[1].split())) == m
preconditions.description: The m affected settlements are distinct.
Each of the n-1 path lines contains exactly two integers.

postconditions.description: Output is a non-negative integer ≤ n, representing the count of possible Book locations.

postconditions.expression: let affected = set(int(p) for p in stdin.splitlines()[1].split()); let paths = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[2:])]; let graph = {i: [] for i in range(1, n+1)}; for a, b in paths: graph[a].append(b); graph[b].append(a); let possible_locations = set(); for loc in range(1, n+1): if all(any(1 <= dist <= d for dist in [BFS_distance(graph, loc, p)]) for p in affected): possible_locations.add(loc); int(stdout.strip()) == len(possible_locations)
postconditions.description: Output is the count of settlements `loc` where, for every affected settlement `p`, the shortest path distance from `loc` to `p` is ≤ d. If no such `loc` exists, output is 0.
